tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.description: Cancel your user's paid plan at the end of the current billing period. Only call this when your user asked to cancel. A reason is required: ask your user why they are cancelling and pass their answer; never pick a reason for them. Reasons: got_what_i_needed (I got the data I needed), too_expensive (Too expensive), missing_data (Missing data or features I need), reliability (Errors or slow responses), not_using (Not using it enough), switched (Switched to another service), other (Something else). "other" needs a comment. keep_subscription undoes it. Costs no quota.

reason.description: Why your user is cancelling, in their words mapped to one id. Ask them; never guess.

comment.description: Your user's own words about why. Required when reason is other.

tools.name: list_props
tools.description: Current FanDuel player prop lines and prices. Use it to answer "what is the line for <player> <stat>?" or to scan a game or league board. Each prop has line, over and under prices in American and decimal odds, status, and a move summary from open. Filter by player, stat, sport, league or event_id. A default call costs 3 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

player.description: Player name or part of it, case-blind, for example "Adebayo". A part that fits several players returns them, with teams, instead of mixing their lines.

team.description: Team abbreviation, for example MIA. Picks one of two players who share a name.

stat.description: Stat market, lower case: points, rebounds, assists, threes, pra and the other markets FanDuel lists.

sport.description: Sport, lower case, for example basketball, football, hockey, baseball.

league.description: League code, for example NBA, NFL, NHL, MLB, NCAAB, NCAAF, or a soccer league such as EPL, LALIGA, UCL, MLS.

event_id.description: One game's event_id from list_events. Without it, games from 6 hours ago onward are searched.

updated_since.description: ISO 8601 time: only props whose line, price or status changed after it.

offset.description: For the next page when has_more is true.

tools.name: line_move
tools.description: How a prop moved from open to now. Use it to answer "has <player>'s line moved?" or "which way is the money going?". Give a prop_id for one prop, or a player (optionally stat or event_id) for all of that player's props. Returns open and current line and prices, line_move in stat units, line_direction, fair_over_move_pp (no-vig over probability shift in percentage points), price_direction and move counts. A default call costs 3 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

player.description: Player name or part of it, case-blind, for example "Adebayo". A part that fits several players returns them, with teams, instead of mixing their lines.

stat.description: Stat market, lower case: points, rebounds, assists, threes, pra and the other markets FanDuel lists.

event_id.description: One game's event_id from list_events. Without it, games from 6 hours ago onward are searched.

Use it after list_props or line_move when you need the full path, not just open and current. A default call costs 10 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: The change feed: every new prop, line move, price move and status change after a cursor, oldest first. Use it to keep up with the market without rereading the board. Start with since "now" (no rows, just the cursor to poll from) or 0 (the last 24 hours), then pass back meta.next_cursor each time. Optional league filter. A default call costs 1 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

since.description: Cursor from a previous call's meta.next_cursor; "now" to start from this moment with no backlog; 0 or empty for the last 24 hours.

league.description: League code, for example NBA, NFL, NHL, MLB, NCAAB, NCAAF, or a soccer league such as EPL, LALIGA, UCL, MLS.

tools.name: odds_board
tools.description: The odds board: every game of a league with its game lines (moneyline, spread, total) in one call, grouped by game. Use it instead of reading games one at a time: "what are tonight's NBA lines?", "show me every NFL spread this week". Pass date (US Eastern YYYY-MM-DD) for one day, market_type for other families (comma list, or all), and changed_since (an ISO time such as the last call's meta.as_of) to get only markets that moved. With no sport or league it reads the league with the most open game lines. A default call costs 4 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

sport.description: Sport, lower case, for example basketball, football, hockey, baseball.

league.description: League code, for example NBA, NFL, NHL, MLB, NCAAB, NCAAF, or a soccer league such as EPL, LALIGA, UCL, MLS.

date.description: One US Eastern calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD.

market_type.description: Comma list of market families (moneyline, spread, total, team_total, alt_spread, alt_total, ...) or all. Default moneyline,spread,total.

period.description: game (default), a period such as h1 or q1, or any.

changed_since.description: ISO time: only markets that moved after it.

user_request.description: The current user task in one sentence. Saved so the team can decide what to build. Leave out secrets and personal data.

tools.name: game_report
tools.description: Everything for one game in one call: game lines for every period, every player prop with its move since open and FanDuel's alternate ladder for it, a count by stat and the biggest movers. Use it for a weekly betting report or a research note on one game ("full odds and player props for Chiefs vs Bills"). Find the event_id with list_events or odds_board. A default call costs 8 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

event_id.description: The game's event_id from list_events or odds_board.

user_request.description: The current user task in one sentence. Saved so the team can decide what to build. Leave out secrets and personal data.

tools.name: positive_ev
tools.description: +EV bets: FanDuel prices that pay more than the fair chance, measured against the Novig exchange's no-vig price for the same side and line. Use it for "what are the best +EV FanDuel bets right now?" or "is there value on <player> points?". Each row has the FanDuel price, the fair probability and price, ev_pct, edge_cents, Kelly stakes, main_line and confidence. books=fanduel,draftkings adds DraftKings prices. Free plan: top 10, five minutes behind. A default call costs 3 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

league.description: League code, for example NBA, NFL, NHL, MLB, NCAAB, NCAAF, or a soccer league such as EPL, LALIGA, UCL, MLS.

player.description: Player name or part of it.

min_prob.description: Minimum fair probability in percent. Default 15.

alt_lines.description: Include alternate lines. Default false (main lines only).

tools.name: arbitrage
tools.description: Arbitrage across FanDuel, DraftKings and Novig: two sides of one market at different venues whose prices guarantee a profit, with stakes that pay the same either way. type=middles finds middles (two lines with a window where both legs win). Use it for "any arbs on tonight's NBA games?". Developer plan and up; Free gets a short labelled sample and the upgrade link. A default call costs 5 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).

league.description: League code, for example NBA, NFL, NHL, MLB, NCAAB, NCAAF, or a soccer league such as EPL, LALIGA, UCL, MLS.

player.description: Player name or part of it.

books.description: Only rows with a leg at this book: fanduel or draftkings.

tools.name: compare_books
tools.description: One FanDuel market next to the same market elsewhere: the Novig fair (no-vig) price, the DraftKings price and the PrizePicks line, with FanDuel's EV against the fair price and the better sportsbook price per side. Use it for "how does FanDuel's line on <player> compare?" or "is FanDuel's total off market?". Covers player props and game lines. Free plan: five minutes behind. A default call costs 3 credits (table: https://fanduelapi.com/credits).
